svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Glucose, C\u2086H\u2081\u2082O\u2086: the main respiratory substrate."], [1, "The straight-chain form has an aldehyde group on carbon 1."], [3, "In water the chain closes into a ring: the oxygen on carbon 5 bonds to carbon 1."], [5.5, "Two isomers: in alpha-glucose the OH on carbon 1 is below the ring; in beta-glucose it is above."], [9, "Two alpha-glucose molecules join by condensation, releasing water."], [12, "The 1,4-glycosidic bond links them: maltose, a disaccharide."]]
svg.title: Glucose: structure and isomers
svg.desc: The open-chain and ring structures of glucose, alpha- and beta-glucose in Haworth projection, and two alpha-glucose joining by condensation to form maltose with a 1,4-glycosidic bond.
svg.text: Glucose: open chain, ring, alpha and beta
Blue numbers: carbon atoms 1 to 6. Thick edge of the ring: towards you.

g.data-info: C₆H₁₂O₆ in its straight form: an aldehyde group (CHO) on carbon 1 and hydroxyl (OH) groups on carbons 2 to 6. In water, more than 99% of glucose is in the ring form.

g.text: O on C5 bonds to C1

g.data-info: The OH on carbon 1 is BELOW the ring. Alpha-glucose forms starch and glycogen.

g.text: OH on C1 below the ring

g.data-info: The OH on carbon 1 is ABOVE the ring. Beta-glucose forms cellulose.

g.text: OH on C1 above the ring

g.data-info: The oxygen of the C5 hydroxyl bonds to carbon 1, closing a six-membered ring with five carbons and one oxygen.
Two alpha-glucose join by condensation: an OH from C1 and an H from the C4 OH form water, leaving a 1,4-glycosidic bond (C–O–C). Hydrolysis breaks it again.

g.text: cellulose: β-glucose, every other one flipped
